annotations.title: What changed since your knowledge cutoff

description: Call this when a user asks about current prices, models or retirements and your knowledge may be out of date: give the date your knowledge ends (YYYY-MM-DD, any date, no key needed) and get a short answer: a one-line summary, the counts of the whole period, and per group the entries a provider's own page or API shows: new models and plans, price changes (old to new, percent, date, source URL), retirements a provider's own lifecycle page dates (effective, and scheduled ones still ahead), and removed plans. kind=llm (LLM API models and inference hosts), gpu, vps or all. The default detail=brief lists first-party entries only (community catalogues such as models.dev and OpenRouter are counted, not listed), at most `limit` per group; detail=full returns every source class and every field (the history window of your key applies; without a key that is the most recent days). Entries carry recorded values only, never a current price: use search_skus or get_price for today's price. Returns an error object for a bad or future date. Retirements come from Azure VM and AWS Bedrock lifecycle pages only (other providers are not parsed). Same data as GET /v1/since and the page /prices/since/<date>. To page through every entry or filter by category use changes_since. Robots.txt changes of AI crawlers are a separate dataset (tool crawlers_changes).

date.description: UTC date, YYYY-MM-DD: the day your knowledge ends, e.g. 2026-06-01
date.title: Date

detail.description: brief (default): a few KB, first-party entries, any date. full: every entry and field, within your history window
detail.title: Detail

kind.description: all (default), llm (LLM API models and inference hosts), gpu or vps
kind.title: Kind

limit.description: Entries per group: 1 to 25 for brief (default 10), 1 to 200 for full (default 25)
limit.title: Limit

name: what_changed_since
